title: latency-profile-async-fused-attn-pipeline
content:
Summary:

This is a running notes doc for an experimental async/fused attention pipeline aimed at reducing 99th-percentile token latency for common seq-len distributions (16/64/256) while retaining cost-efficient throughput. The focus is on combining an async staging layer for KV pages + lightweight fusion of attention read paths (masking + rotary + dropout bypass) with FlashAttention-style matmul kernels.

Goals:
- Reduce tail latency for short/medium sequences (target: 10-25% P99 improvement for seq<=64).
- Keep memory working set small for pinned-page KV model (paged KV).
- Provide heuristics for when to use aggressive fusion vs. conservative fallback.

Motivation / Observed problem:
- Current FlashAttention integration gives excellent average throughput but P99 suffers when paged KV has misses and we stall to load pages.
- Synchronous page loads block the critical token path; attempts to hide this with larger batches increase latency for interactive workloads.
- Some fused ops (rotary + mask + scale) add per-token branching costs that show up on small sequences due to kernel launch overheads.

Design idea overview (high level):
1) Async staging layer: stage KV page loads onto a dedicated CUDA stream per-GPU that can prefetch predicted pages using request metadata (session hot-set).
2) Double-buffered attention pipeline: while current tokens are being inference-attended on stream0, stream1 prepares the next KV chunk + computes partial matmuls for heads that have all KV resident.
3) Lightweight fusion: fuse masking + rotary + dropout-bypass into the matmul epilogue for the common path; keep an unfused safe path for cases with page faults or quantization fallbacks.
4) Heuristic router: decide per-request whether to use fused-async fast path or conservative fallback (sync KV + unfused kernels) based on: hit_probability, seq_len, batch_size, latency SLO class.

Microbench setup (how we measured):
- HW: A100 80GB, CUDA 12.2, cuBLASLt, custom build FlashAttention2 fork (local) with our epilogue hooks.
- Models: 1.3B and 7B float16 variants, kv page size = 64 tokens per page.
- Workloads: three mixes: short (seq=16, 8 requests/s), medium (seq=64, 16 req/s), long (seq=256, 4 req/s).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for token generation, CPU-GPU kernel overlap time, page load latency distribution, GPU occupancy.

Key microbench findings (raw):
- Baseline (sync page load + standard flashattn epilogue):    seq16 P99 = 28.3 ms  | seq64 P99 = 52.1 ms
- Async-stage + unfused kernels:                              seq16 P99 = 20.5 ms  | seq64 P99 = 45.8 ms
- Async-stage + fused epilogue (rotary+mask fused):          seq16 P99 = 16.9 ms  | seq64 P99 = 38.0 ms
- Aggressive double-buffering + fusion (best config):        seq16 P99 = 15.8 ms  | seq64 P99 = 35.5 ms
- Throughput trade: peak throughput drops ~6-9% when fusion is enabled for long sequences due to reduced kernel reuse (but latency improves for short seq).

Interpretation / patterns:
- Fusion benefits short sequences the most: kernel launch and epilogue overhead dominates there. Fusing removes the additional kernel for rotary/mask and saves a cudaLaunch per token batch.
- Async staging hides ~60-80% of page load latency for predicted hot-set pages; misses still cause spikes.
- Double-buffering reduces synchronization stalls but increases overall GPU memory transient usage by ~8%. Acceptable for A100 80GB; borderline for 40GB class for large models.

Kernel-level notes (implementation sketch):
- Matmul kernel: use existing flashattn fused matmul but add an "epilogue flags" bitmask per head indicating whether to apply rotary/mask/dropout in-epilogue or defer.
- Epilogue pseudo-code (C-like):

  for (i in lane) {
    float o = acc[i];
    if (epilogue_flags & ROTARY) o = apply_rotary(o, pos);
    if (epilogue_flags & MASK) { if (mask[pos]==0) o = -INF; }
    // dropout is usually bypassed on inference; provide slot if needed
    out[i] = post_scale(o, scale);
  }

- Use warp-level primitives to broadcast mask bits to lanes to avoid divergent branches in epilogue. Pack mask in 32-bit words for quick checks.
- For quantized paths (4-bit qkv), keep unfused path for correctness; fusion only on fp16/fp32 for now.

Paged-KV scheduling heuristics (draft):
- Maintain per-session hot-score (LRU-ish with recency and frequency), updated in CPU control plane.
- Prefetch if hot_score > H and predicted next tokens > T (configurable).
- If batch contains mixed hot and cold sessions, split into two micro-batches: hot->fast-path, cold->slow-path. This keeps tail low for interactive sessions.
- Eviction policy: prefer LRU at page-level but tie-break by estimated next-access distance (based on N-gram tokens and simple Markov predictor).

Async pipeline notes (implementation):
- Use one dedicated stream per GPU for page IO and memcpy; use cudaMemcpyAsync + pinned host staging buffer.
- Map page load completion to a CUDA event; matmul kernel checks event with cudaStreamWaitEvent to coordinate when safe to read KV data. Avoid busy-waiting.
- If event not satisfied before SLO cutoff, router marks request to fallback path (sync load) to avoid indefinite stall.

Failure modes observed:
- Over-aggressive prefetching causes memory thrash for high-concurrency workloads -> increases overall latency. Need prefetch budget per-GPU.
- Fusion code path has subtle numerical differences vs unfused baseline when using mixed precision + layernorm epsilon differences; observed tiny logits drift (<1e-4) but worth regression tests.

Heuristic knobs (config):
- prefetch_budget_per_gpu: int (max pages to prefetch concurrently)
- hot_threshold_H: float (0-1)
- buffer_count: 1 or 2 (double-buffer toggle)
- fusion_enabled: bool (global)
- fusion_min_seq_len: int (don't fuse if seq > X to preserve throughput)

Regression / testing plan:
- Add unit test to compare fused epilogue outputs vs unfused within tolerance for multiple seeds.
- Synthetic stress tests: many sessions with alternating hot/cold to validate eviction budget.
- Perf CI: record p50/p95/p99 across small/medium/large sequences on A100 and 40GB 8x setups.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Better predictor for next-page access (n-gram vs RNN lightweight predictor). TODO: prototype a 1-layer LSTM predictor in Python and evaluate hit-rate improvement.
- Can we safely extend fusion to 4-bit qkv with per-tile dequant in-epilogue? Complexity vs gain unclear.
- What is the right default prefetch_budget for Dedicated customers vs Hosted? Should be per-tier.

Immediate action items:
- Diego: PR for epilogue flags and warp-level mask broadcast (github PR linked).
- Evelyn: build perf harness to reproduce microbench above on 40GB machines.
- Ravi: prototype page-prediction LSTM using recent session traces (dataset in internal store).
- Asha: add perf regression scripts + add test in CI gating PRs that touch fused epilogue.

Notes-to-self / random observations:
- On short sequences, kernel launch overhead ~1.2-1.6 ms per launch on A100; combining epilogues is the low-hanging fruit.
- Consider a hybrid epilogue that unrolls small seqs to avoid warp underutilization.

References / links inlined above.

Status: still experimental. Recommend gating on thorough numerical regression + perf CI before enabling globally.

End of doc.
